title: Credentials stay outside source
summary: Jenkins can provide credentials through configured bindings. A job should request only what it needs and avoid printing secret values.
introduction: Jenkins can provide credentials through configured bindings. A job should request only what it needs and avoid printing secret values. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Jenkins can provide credentials through configured bindings. A job should request only what it needs and avoid printing secret values.

blocks.code:
Jenkinsfile: names an approved credential binding
Credential store: holds the secret
Step: uses it for the authorised job only
blocks.title: Credentials stay outside source

blocks.text: The file contains a reference, not the secret itself. Binding syntax depends on the configured credential type and plugins.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why a secret should not be pasted into a build log.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Masking log output is not permission to expose secrets to untrusted code.
For more detail later, use this [Jenkins further reading](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/).
